newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portucel says expects good second half.
newsitem.headline: Portucel says expects good second half.

text.p: Portuguese pulp group Portucel Industrial-Empresa Produtora de Celulose said that the international conditions were right for the company to perform well in the second half of the year.

Portucel, which announced a 752 million profit for the first half of 1997 after a 2.9 billion escudo loss over the same 1996 period, said that the improving international economy and falling world stock levels were creating a favourable business environment.
"Demand and supply have progressively moved into balance... creating the conditions for a favourable performance by Portucel in the second half of the year," it said in a statement.

It said the balance had been struck with a reduction in the volume of announced new international capacity. NorScan stocks stood at 1.57 million tonnes at the end of June, a figure which it described as "healthy."
"The production of Bleached Eucalyptus Kraft Pulp (BEKP) has evolved favourably, allowing favourable levels of stocks and high rates of capacity utilisation," it said.
